Q: Unable to import pyspark.pipelines module A:

You are trying to run the command on a generic notebook as a generic pyspark import.

The pipeline module can be accessed only within a context of a pipeline.

Q: What is a "channel" in Monolog logger? A:

In simple words, you can define a channel as a separate log file.

Generally you might need to classify your log files for different services or modules.

For this purpose, Monolog allows you to create different channels, where each can log separately to different file and allow you to configure your log per channel.

In the line you are referring to 

 $logger = new MonologLogger('channel-name'); 
 $app->container->logger = $logger;

You are specifying the channel in the constructor of Monologger.

Anytime you use this $logger object it will be writing to the file you specified when you configured the channel. Below is an example from the Symfony docs for a channel config

https://symfony.com/doc/current/logging/channels_handlers.html#switching-a-channel-to-a-different-handler

   monolog:
      handlers:
          security:
             # log all messages (since debug is the lowest level)
             level:    debug
             type:     stream
             path:     '%kernel.logs_dir%/security.log'
             channels: [security]

In which case you would do that in your code to use the channel

 $logger = new MonologLogger('security');

And then you will be logging to "security.log" with type "stream" errors of level "debug".

Q: Reusing built query with one less join in CodeIgniter A:

First, I don't see the point of JOINing the favorite table (or any tables) because you are only selecting the main table's columns with outfit_main.*. If you are optionally filtering with a WHERE clause condition on the favorite table, then just use a LEFT JOIN.

Second, CodeIgniter's result() method doesn't return false; it returns an array of zero or more objects.

Third, instead of potentially making two trips to the database, make just one "loose" trip and then execute your filtering logic in PHP.

$result = $this->db
    ->distinct()
    ->select('om.*, f.product_id fav_prod_id')
    ->join('outfit_products op', 'om.id = op.outfit_id')                                 
    ->join('product p', 'op.product_id = p.id')
    ->join('favorite f', 'f.product_id = op.product_id', 'left')
    ->get('outfit_main om')
    ->result();  

return array_values(
    array_filter(
        $result,
        fn($obj) => $obj->fav_prod_id !== null
    )
)
?: $result;

The above will return only rows with non-null product ids in the favorites table unless there are no records withon-nulls, in which case the unfiltered records will be returned.

Finally, if you truly just want to optionally make a second trip to the database, you can clone the query builder object before before joining the favorite table, and then fallback to that cached builder if the favorite-joined query yields no records.

$this->db
    ->distinct()
    ->select('om.*, f.product_id fav_prod_id')
    ->from('outfit_main om')
    ->join('outfit_products op', 'om.id = op.outfit_id')                                 
    ->join('product p', 'op.product_id = p.id');

$fallback = clone $this->db;

return $this->db
    ->join('favorite f', 'f.product_id = op.product_id')
    ->get()
    ->result()
?: $fallback
    ->get()
    ->result();

I've never needed to clone a query in my professional codebases and I didn't test this, but I assume this is a working implementation.

Q: How to fix 'SQLite exception, Insufficient parameters supplied to the command' when using INSERT statement A:

I had this problem when updating to version 1.0.118 of System.Data.Sqlite. From this version onward, the parameters are case-sensitive:

SQLiteCommand command = 
      new SQLiteCommand(“insert into bridge (id, engWord) values (@id, @engWord)”,cnn);

This works:

command.Parameters.AddWithValue(“engWord”, br.engWord)

This does not work:

command.Parameters.AddWithValue(“engword”, br.engWord)
